title: introduce-telemetry-sidecar-prefetch-metrics-and-seasonal-alert-gate
author: Maya Chen
description: Add a lightweight telemetry sidecar that runs alongside inference workers to emit compact per-invocation telemetry and prefetch effectiveness metrics, plus a seasonal alert gating mechanism that reduces noisy paging during predictable diurnal traffic patterns. Motivation: customers are experiencing noisy alert churn tied to predictable daily token-usage seasonality and prefetch warmup bursts; we need a low-latency, low-cost way to (1) surface per-invocation kernel-queue-depth, prefetch-hit/miss signals, and estimated energy/token proxies, and (2) apply context-aware alert gating so SREs can focus on non-seasonal anomalies. This PR implements: 1) sidecar binary and a tiny protobuf-over-UDP wire format optimized for 1kB/second telemetry per worker, 2) per-invocation prefetched-prefix metrics (prefetch_hit, prefetch_latency_ms, kv_prefetch_age_ms) and kernel_queue_depth sampled at entry/exit, 3) a new histogram metric token_energy_estimate_bytes that uses a compact bucketing scheme to approximate GPU work per-token for coarse cost attribution, 4) an alert-gate policy engine that ingests seasonal baseline windows (hour-of-day, day-of-week) and mutes low-severity token-cost alerts within expected bands while allowing bursts above a configurable multiplier, 5) DB migration to add telemetry_sidecar_config and seasonal_windows tables, 6) console dashboard: "Sidecar Prefetch Overview" and a lightweight "Seasonal Alert Gate" playbook panel. Backwards compatibility: sidecar is optional; servers without sidecar fall back to existing runtime metrics with a small compatibility shim that synthesizes kernel_queue_depth as -1 and prefetch_* as unknown. Tests: unit tests for sidecar encoder/decoder, integration test that spins a local worker+sidecar and validates emitted metrics reach the metrics-relay, and an end-to-end staging run with sample seasonal windows to verify alert suppression. Rollout plan: 1) deploy sidecar to staging and run for 48h, 2) enable seasonal-window read-only mode in prod to validate no missed critical alerts for 7 days, 3) flip suppression to active with conservative multipliers, monitor for 14 days, 4) iterate on buckets and multipliers by observation. Related: ENG-4412 (prefetch telemetry exploration), ENG-4470 (alert noisefloor initiative).

review_thread: Diego Alvarez (2024-11-08): Can we guarantee the sidecar's failure mode is crash-only and won't block the worker? Maya Chen: Yes, sidecar communicates over UDP and the shim uses a 50ms deadline; worker proceeds if ack not received.

Priya Nair (2024-11-09): The seasonal windows schema looks flexible but do we need timezone normalization? Maya Chen: Windows are stored in UTC and UI converts by tenant timezone; added UTC note to migration comment.

Ruth Kim (2024-11-10): Prefer exponential histogram for token_energy_estimate, but I see compact manual buckets—can we revisit? Maya Chen: Chose manual small set to keep cardinality low; added an adapter to convert to exponential histograms downstream for analysis.
Ruth Kim (2024-11-11): LGTM pending one nit on migration idempotency. Maya Chen: fixed migration to be idempotent and added test.
Diego Alvarez (2024-11-12): CI flaked on lint; re-run looks clean. Diego Alvarez: Approved.
release_notes: Add optional telemetry sidecar to emit per-invocation prefetch and kernel queue metrics
Introduce seasonal alert gate to suppress predictable low-severity alert noise
New console dashboard: Sidecar Prefetch Overview
